answer: Cheap throwaway identities cannot reuse work, so an attacker must buy and register real relics per sock-puppet, multiplying cost linearly. Each agent must stake a relic bound to a verified hardware identity, then solve a per-epoch challenge whose answer is salted with that relic's signature. Peers cross-check results against a shared oasis of prior epoch proofs, and any identity seen in a mirror of duplicated work is slashed. Faking one identity costs a full stake plus lost compute, making mass sybils economically irrational. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
